paper_summary: Silicone-rubber (Smooth-On Mold Star 30) syntactic foams were hand-mixed and cast with 3M A16/500 (GB500) and A20/1000 (GB1000) glass bubbles at 10, 20 and 30 wt%, giving densities from 748 down to 360 kg/m3 versus 1120 kg/m3 for the neat resin (a 63-68% reduction at 30 wt%). Quasi-static compression was run at room temperature on virgin specimens and on specimens heat treated by holding one face at 500 C for 1 h. Increasing glass-bubble content raised the plateau stress and lengthened the plateau (crush) region, improving energy absorption, while the 500 C treatment produced a brittle heat-resistant surface layer (two-layer structure) without considerably changing the compression response.

structure.microstructure_notes: Closed-cell syntactic foam, glass bubbles dispersed in silicone rubber. After one-sided 500 C / 1 h exposure the foam becomes a two-layer structure: a white, brittle, heat-resistive front layer extending less than 1/3 of the section height and a back layer that stays elastic/plastic like the unheated foam; SEM shows the glass bubbles remain intact at 500 C (they rupture at 750 C). Steady-state back-face temperature 130 C.

extraction_notes: Densities converted from kg/m3 to g/cm3 (Table II divided by 1000). Weight percentages converted to fractions (particle_weight_fraction); volume fractions are not reported and were not computed because the paper does not give the resin density needed together with a stated mixing rule. All compression results (stress-strain curves, plateau stress, densification strain, energy absorption) appear only as plots in Figs. 2 and 4 with no numeric values in text or tables, so every Properties field is null; the records carry composition, density and test-condition metadata only. strain_rate_per_s = 0.00098 1/s was derived from the stated 1 mm/min crosshead speed and 17 mm specimen height (1/60 mm/s / 17 mm); it is not stated as a strain rate in the paper. cure_or_process_temperature_c is 25 C for the virgin foams (6 h room-temperature cure) and 500 C for the heat-treated foams (one face held at 500 +/- 10 C for 1 h); all compression tests themselves were done at room temperature, so test.temperature_c is 25 C for every record. The neat silicone rubber resin reference (1120 kg/m3) contains no hollow particles and was not recorded. The 0.06-0.16 W/(m K) thermal conductivity in Table I is a property of the glass bubbles quoted from the 3M datasheet, not a measured foam property, so it was not entered. Glass-bubble crush pressures (3.44 and 6.90 MPa) are supplier particle data and are recorded in particle_grade rather than as foam strength.
